title: Astor vs. Perplexity Finance: research tool or personal investing agent?
summary: Perplexity Finance is a strong research tool that can read your holdings. Astor is a personal investing agent and SEC-registered adviser.
body_markdown:
### Is Perplexity Finance free?


Much of it is. Perplexity Finance’s market pages are free to browse, and Perplexity said at launch that standard (free) users could link a portfolio and use the basic Portfolio page. Advanced Computer features are for Pro and Max subscribers, which cost $17 and $167 a month billed annually as of October 2026.


### Can Perplexity Finance see my brokerage account?


Yes, if you’re in the US or Canada and you link it through Plaid. Perplexity says the connection is read-only, so it can see your holdings but can’t trade or move money. You can then ask questions about your portfolio or have Computer build dashboards on top of it.


### Is Perplexity Finance a financial adviser?


Perplexity says its finance data is for informational purposes only and isn’t intended as investment advice. Astor is an SEC-registered investment adviser, so its recommendations are personalized investment advice and it owes clients a fiduciary duty.


### What’s a good Perplexity Finance alternative for watching my portfolio?


If you want research, Perplexity is already one of the strongest options, in our view. If you want something that watches the portfolio you already have and gives you personalized advice, look at a personal investing agent like Astor, which connects to your accounts, texts you when something matters, and leaves every decision to you. Our guide to[AI investing apps that work with your brokerage](https://www.astor.app/blog/ai-investing-apps-that-work-with-your-brokerage) covers more options.


### Does Astor trade for me?


No. Astor can see the holdings in your connected accounts, but it can’t move money or place trades in them. With Text to Trade, you approve every trade, the order executes in your own Robinhood agentic account, and the agent can only use the money you set aside for it.
